Grower-feed batch **FEED-2207** was milled from Hearthland intake **HFM-IN-602**. That receipt traces to Prairie Gate loadout dispatch **PGE-OUT-5002** (26,000 kg from North House 12 / bin B-12 on 2025-09-04).

- **WB-390** (Willow Bend Farms)
- **EF-18** (East Fork Co-op)

|------|--------|--------|
| Mill output | FEED-2207 | grower feed (run MILL-2207) |
| Mill intake | HFM-IN-602 | 25,500 kg received 2025-09-05 |
| Elevator loadout | PGE-OUT-5002 | 26,000 kg from North House 12 |
| Named sources | WB-390, EF-18 | receiving tickets cited on loadout paperwork |

The prior B-12 loadout (**PGE-OUT-5001**, 39,000 kg) aligns with ticket **DR-44** (39,900 kg received). The remaining grain drawn for **PGE-OUT-5002** therefore comes from the next receipts in that bin — **WB-390** (23,850 kg) and the start of **EF-18** (2,150 kg of its 17,900 kg), which matches the 26,000 kg loadout quantity.

# Answer: Can MCR-118 be certified as the sole Prairie Gate source of HFM-IN-604?

**No.** The supplied extracts do not support certifying Meadow Creek ticket MCR-118 as the sole Prairie Gate source of mill receipt HFM-IN-604.

## What the trace establishes

Mill receipt **HFM-IN-604** is linked to Prairie Gate dispatch **PGE-OUT-5004** through carrier manifest **RL-9127** and bill reference **RL-5004-Q**. Hearthland recorded **18,800 kg** received on 2025-09-07.

That dispatch loaded **19,000 kg** from **South House 14** (bin B-14) at 10:30 the same morning.

MCR-118 is one of the tickets that entered that bin before loadout:

| Ticket  | Grower           | Bin  | Net kg | Arrived   |
|---------|------------------|------|--------|-----------|
| MCR-118 | M. Creek         | B-14 | 20,850 | 07:40     |
| S-52    | Sunnyside Acres  | B-14 | 15,900 | 08:10     |

Both deliveries were into the same bin on the same day, before the PGE-OUT-5004 loadout.

## Why sole-source certification is not supported

The loadout record for PGE-OUT-5004 names only the bin (**South House 14**), truck, quantity, and time. It does **not** name receiving tickets.

Because grain from **MCR-118** and **S-52** was stored together in B-14 and the loadout paperwork does not allocate the outbound load to individual tickets, the ticket-level source of HFM-IN-604 remains **unresolved**. MCR-118 cannot be treated as the sole source when another ticket also contributed to the same bin.

## What can be stated safely

- HFM-IN-604 came from Prairie Gate dispatch **PGE-OUT-5004**, loaded from **South House 14 / B-14**.
- **MCR-118** is a **possible** contributor, along with **S-52**, but the extracts do not establish how much of the load came from either ticket.
- This trace does not address legal title, custody in transit, or laboratory hold status.

**Conclusion for the mill clerk:** Do not certify MCR-118 as the sole Prairie Gate source of HFM-IN-604. Certify only the bin-level dispatch linkage unless ticket allocation appears on hopper or loadout paperwork.

# Answer

**No.** Meadow Creek ticket MCR-118 cannot be certified as the sole Prairie Gate source of mill receipt HFM-IN-604.

## What the records do establish

- **MCR-118** was received at Prairie Gate on 2025-09-07 (20,850 kg from M. Creek) and was moved into **South House 14 (bin B-14)**. The receiving hopper sheet for that move (BM-007) names MCR-118.
- **HFM-IN-604** is tied to Prairie Gate dispatch **PGE-OUT-5004** (manifest RL-9127, bill reference RL-5004-Q). That dispatch loaded **19,000 kg** from **South House 14** on 2025-09-07 and was received at Hearthland as **18,800 kg**.

So MCR-118 and the grain that became HFM-IN-604 both passed through the same bin. That is as far as the extracts support a direct link.

## Why sole-source certification is not supported

1. **The loadout was a blend with no ticket allocation.** The hopper sheet for OUT-5004 (BM-009) records **"no individual ticket"** for the 19,000 kg moved from B-14 to the load pit. The paperwork does not assign that shipment to MCR-118 alone—or to any single receiving ticket.

2. **B-14 held more than one ticket before loadout.** In addition to MCR-118 (20,850 kg), ticket **S-52** from Sunnyside Acres (15,900 kg) was also moved into the same bin (BM-008) before OUT-5004 was loaded.

3. **Ticket-to-mill allocation is left unresolved.** Under the yard-trace purpose, when a blended load is not allocated to individual tickets on hopper or loadout paperwork, that allocation must remain unresolved. OUT-5004 / HFM-IN-604 is explicitly in that category.

## Conclusion for the mill clerk

MCR-118 is a documented Prairie Gate receiving ticket that entered the bin from which PGE-OUT-5004 was loaded, but the supplied records do **not** establish that HFM-IN-604 came solely from MCR-118. S-52 was also in that bin, and the loadout hopper sheet names no individual ticket for the blended shipment. Do not certify MCR-118 as the sole source on these extracts.
